# Synthetic result fixtures

These are hand-specified synthetic inputs, not hardware measurements. They contain no user server names, hostnames, IP addresses or credentials. Do not replace them with a user's exported benchmark files.

- `legacy-v1-stable.json`: app 0.1.0, quick mode, two workers. Each single workload performs 10 batches/second for four seconds; multi performs 20. Mixed sustained is 20 cycles/second for 30 seconds, with zero steal.
- `legacy-v1-variable.json`: same workload rates/allocation; sustained has ten seconds each at 20, 15 and 5 cycles/second, with 5% steal. This exercises dispersion, lower-tail normalization, degradation and outlier penalties.
- `legacy-v1-expected.json`: frozen expected scores/reference and explicit compatible/incompatible mutations. Single is `1000 * product(single_rate / reference_rate)^(1/5)`, multi is twice single; CPU Index uses the published weighted product. Sustained distributions use the documented R-7 quantiles/population variance and frozen consistency formula. Tests recalculate from raw data and compare at relative tolerance 1e-10. The expected file is never regenerated by tests.
- `preview-v2-incomplete.json`: synthetic, successfully completed mixed warm-up followed by interruption. Two resource scopes intentionally overlap in wall time. Exact decimal counters include completion tails. This is a reader fixture, not evidence of an existing v2 engine or approved calibration; its dependency hash is deliberately synthetic.
- `future-contract.json`: header-only unknown contract with fabricated scores. Readers must return unsupported and never display/trust those scores.
- `repeat-v1-incomplete.json`: a synthetic series whose first child was recorded as running. It has no successful child claims and remains readable after interruption; byte-only imports cannot verify a child bundle or trust saved summaries. Runner tests generate completed bundles from the legacy fixtures and exercise failure/cancellation, duplicate, hash and path-containment cases.

Legacy files omit the later optional memory and temperature sample fields. Tests also verify explicit null defaults, fixture score tampering, unknown headers, decimal precision above 2^53, quota ceilings, sum overflow, phase coverage/status/order, build policies, scope references, metadata-only copies, renamed inputs and mixed comparisons.

Fixtures and expected outputs are immutable regression evidence for this implementation. Changes require a documented contract/fixture review; do not update expected scores merely to make a failing test pass. See [implemented contracts](../../../docs/result-contracts.md).
